_note: Settings for running a corpus incident (scripts/run_incident.py). caps_usd are the per-configuration caps per incident: since 2026-10-25 an equal hard cap of USD 0.50 for the hierarchy and both single-model baselines, which supersedes D2's 0.10 and 1.00 (docs/DECISIONS.md, Equal benchmark caps). context_sources are the sources the director reads in full for its diagnosis. The catalog is data for these runs only; prices and latencies are placeholders, not measured.

baselines._note: The single-model baselines (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, Benchmark design): (b) on Ultra and (c) on Lightning. Each reads every slice with the operators' prompt, skills and findings model, then writes the diagnosis; no plan, no managers, no auditor model, no escalation ladder and no reassignment. roles_by_source picks the operator role (and so its skill) for a source; every other source uses default_role. cap names the entry of caps_usd.
baselines.instruction: Report what this slice shows about the incident in the goal: errors, changes and anything that points to its root cause, citing single lines.

benchmark._note: The benchmark plan for scripts/run_benchmark.py: every (incident, configuration, repeat) runs once, one after another. configurations: a the hierarchy, b and c the single-model baselines above. caps_usd is each configuration's run cap for the benchmark: USD 0.50 for a, b and c alike (2026-10-25, the same as caps_usd above). An incident's split comes from its ground_truth.json: test-split incidents run live only with --freeze-confirmed, once tuning has ended. Results (metrics only, no prompt text) go to results_dir, cassettes (with prompt text, gitignored) to cassette_dir.

goal: Investigate the incident described in ticket.md: find its root cause and its category, cite the evidence line by line, and propose a remediation plan.
